Introducing ExtractBenchPro: the most challenging benchmark for real-world document extraction.

We see a massive long tail of document complexity in terms of use cases brought on from our customers, that are completely unsolved from a price-performance standpoint. These include trial balances, well logs, canvass binders, site plan reviews, duty reconciliations, loss runs, and more.

Most existing extraction benchmarks are saturated by the frontier models (our cheapest modes now score 93%+ on ExtractBench). So there is enormous economic value in building a complex extraction benchmark that reflects this long-tail of knowledge work.

We spent a long time curating the most complex elements that we saw from real world extraction use cases:
✅ Document conventions: containing legends or rules where the rest of the document should be interpreted
✅ Density of internal jargon: specific definitions that must be cross-referenced within a doc
✅ Aggregation and reasoning: beyond returning exact values on a page, infer values derived from aggregating multiple sources of information
✅ Drawn relations: complex diagrams like procedures and circuits
✅ Charts inside documents: read precise points within a chart
✅ Long chart sheets: some data series like well logs cram all this data into an extremely long page

Within the industries where document extraction is relevant, even small mistakes can have enormous negative impacts. Therefore our headline evaluation metric is based on perfect documents: the proportion of docs with perfect (100%) value f1 score.
(Besides this we also measure value f1 and grounded f1)

It’s an extremely hard task for even the latest frontier models to solve, topping out at ~58% or so in Value F1 score for Codex with Astra - which is quite good but extremely expensive (almost $1 per page!) Our LlamaParse agentic/agentic plus modes are 20-40% and cover the left side of the Pareto frontier, at price ranges that are feasible for full production use.

ExtractBenchPro is available today as a website/technical blog, and also on Github and HuggingFace. Check it out!

reviewedPosts.text:
Agent 自己改 Harness，最难的其实并不是「怎么改」。

而在于没有标准答案时，怎么知道这次改动到底有没有变好。

Google 团队这篇 Harness²，专门研究开放世界里的 Harness 自进化。

它设计了两层递归。

第一层针对当前任务：先提出 Harness 修改，再让新旧版本在相同条件下执行，通过行为差异判断哪些改动值得保留。

也就是说，它不依赖 ground-truth verifier，也能用真实执行结果来指导修改。

第二层更有意思：

每次改 Harness 的过程也会被总结成经验，记录什么问题、用了什么修改、为什么有效，再拿去指导未来的新任务。

所以它积累的，不只是更好的 Harness，还有「怎么改 Harness」这件事本身。

在 WorkBuddy-Bench、JobBench 和法律 Agent Benchmark 上，单轮改进就能稳定提升 GLM-5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash，最高分别提升 11.5、4.5 和 11.8 个百分点；继续增加递归预算，表现还能进一步上涨。

我更关注第二层递归。

单次把 Agent 调得更好并不难，真正接近长期自进化的，是系统开始积累「过去怎么把自己调好」的经验。

Harness² 往前走的一步，就是让改进机制本身也开始有记忆。
